text: Tarski intended his semantic conception of truth — with its material adequacy condition, the T-schema — to be a fully metaphysical version of the correspondence theory of truth.
explanation: This is false. Tarski's definition is immanent to a particular language and is fixed by the requirement that a theory of truth entail every instance of the T-schema ('S' is true iff S); it takes no stand on the metaphysics of facts or of a correspondence relation. That neutrality is precisely why both deflationists and correspondence theorists have each claimed the T-schema in support of their opposed positions.
